mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (current value: 0.08%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because low interest rates reduce the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, increasing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (current value: 0.08%) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 280.0 (current value: 281.933) signals high inflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because high inflation erodes corporate profit margins and increases the risk premium on equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL > 280.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.5% and CPIAUCSL is below 285.0 (current values: FEDFUNDS=0.08%, CPIAUCSL=281.933), the real interest rate is low, which compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5 AND CPIAUCSL < 285.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 4.5%), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because high unemployment signals weak economic activity, reducing corporate earnings growth and increasing the risk of recession.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE > 4.5 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A PAYEMS value above 140000 (current value: 149629.0) signals strong labor market conditions, which are associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because strong employment growth supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when PAYEMS > 140000 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: HOUST above 1700 (current value: 1702.0) signals strong housing market activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because a strong housing market indicates robust consumer spending and economic growth, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when HOUST > 1700.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above 100.0 and GDP (GDPC1) is above 19800.0 (current values: INDPRO=101.8926, GDPC1=19805.962), the economy is in a strong growth regime, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This is because strong industrial output and GDP growth signal robust economic activity, supporting corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when INDPRO > 100.0 AND GDPC1 > 19800.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a weak housing market regime (HOUST < 1700.0), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This is because weak housing activity signals reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown, which depresses equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when HOUST < 1700.0 over the last 5 years.
